raw_response:
I am 63 years old, been farming these 8 mu in Quzhou for 40 years. Never went to school, but I know this land with my hands. Me and my old woman, we work it ourselves. Last year I put 6 mu in spring maize and 2 mu in mungbean, and that is what I will do again this year. I do not change what works.

For the maize, I buy hybrid seed from the township shop — the same kind Old Wang across the road plants. I put about 3 jin of seed per mu. At planting time, I spread one full 50-jin bag of compound fertilizer on every mu. The bag says 15-15-15 on it. That is what I have always done. Then when the maize gets up to my knee, I top-dress with half a bag of urea per mu — 25 jin. Last year I tried to save money and skipped the urea on one plot, and the cobs came out half empty. Never again. Compound fertilizer is 150 yuan a bag now, urea is 100 yuan, but a bad harvest means we go hungry. Wasted fertilizer just means less cash in my pocket. I would rather put down too much than too little.

I will water the maize three times. First right after planting, to wake the seeds up. Second when the tassels come out. Third when the grain is filling. My well pump runs on diesel, so I do not water for nothing. For bugs, I spray twice — once when the seedlings are small for those cutworms that chew them off at night, and once when the ears are forming for the corn borers. Each spray costs about 30 yuan per mu for the medicine. I pay the tractor man 30 yuan per mu to rotary till before planting. At my age, I am not turning that soil with a shovel anymore.

For the 2 mu of mungbean, I plant seeds I saved from last year — the old local kind, not those fancy new ones from the shop. I spread about 15 jin of compound fertilizer per mu at planting. That is enough. Mungbean does not eat fertilizer like maize does, and my father always said it makes its own nitrogen. I will water twice, maybe three times if the sky gives us no rain for a month. One spray for aphids. If the year is kind, I get about 100 jin per mu. Sometimes 120.

I watch what my neighbors do. If Old Wang puts more fertilizer, I think about it. If he puts less, I do not follow. Two old people cannot manage more than 8 mu, and I do not hire labor — it costs too much. Every yuan I spend on fertilizer is a yuan I cannot spend on medicine or diesel, so I count it all. But I have learned: better safe than hungry.

decision.reasoning_summary: I have farmed this 8 mu for 40 years with no schooling, so I copy what worked last year and what my neighbors do. I plant 6 mu of hybrid spring maize and 2 mu of traditional mungbean. For maize, I apply one 50-jin bag of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer and half a bag of urea per mu, irrigate three times, spray twice for bugs, and rotary till — fertilizer is expensive but a bad harvest is a disaster, so I would rather over-apply than risk empty cobs. For mungbean, I use only 15 jin of compound fertilizer per mu, water twice, and spray once, because mungbean is light-feeding and I save my own seed. Me and my wife do all the labor except hiring the tractor, and every yuan spent on inputs is a yuan not spent elsewhere, so I count carefully but never cut where it risks the yield.
